docs.title: Blender 5.1 NPR Port - New Features & Usage Guide
Project Introduction
docs.text:
Blender 5.1 NPR Port is an NPR-specialized Blender fork that combines features from Goo Engine and 4.4 NPR-prototype with additional useful specialty nodes.

Most features are Eevee exclusive and do not support Cycles.

docs.title: Documentation Scope
docs.text: This documentation covers NPR/Eevee extension features that have been added to Blender 5.1 NPR Port compared to official Blender 5.1 and currently exist in this branch, as well as their basic usage methods.

docs.title: 1. Scene-Level Eevee Extensions
docs.text:
• Render Textures - Scene-level additional render texture system
  • Filter Materials - Full-screen filter stack

docs.title: 2. Shader Nodes (20+ new nodes)
docs.text:
• Render Info, Scene Time, Screen Derivative
  • Portal In/Out, Screenspace Info
  • World Environment, Bevel, Curvature
  • Shader Info, Light Info, Scene Color

docs.title: 3. NPR Tree Workflow
docs.text:
• NPR Input/Output nodes
  • Per-light processing
  • Built-in node group assets

docs.title: 4. Interface & Settings
docs.text:
• Material preview control
  • World environment configuration
  • Light group management

Eevee Only

All NPR Port features require the Eevee render engine. Cycles is not supported.

Ready to explore? Check out the sections below for more information!

docs.title: Extended Shader Nodes
docs.text: This page documents 20+ new shader nodes added to Blender 5.1 NPR Port.

docs.title: Render Info Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Access post-render image properties

Outputs: - Frag Coord - Fragment/pixel coordinates (X, Y, Z, W) - Width - Render target width (pixels) - Height - Render target height (pixels)

Usage: Use in calculations that require screen resolution or pixel position.

docs.title: Scene Time Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Access time-based values for animation

Outputs: - Frame - Current frame number - Seconds - Elapsed time (seconds) - Timeline - Timeline position - Scaled Frame - Custom-scaled frame number

Usage: Create time-based animations and effects.

docs.title: Screen Derivative Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Detect edges and gradients in screen space

Inputs: - Value - Input to differentiate

Outputs: - DDX - X direction derivative - DDY - Y direction derivative - DDXY - Combined derivatives

Usage: Edge detection, gradient mapping, post-process effects.

docs.title: Light Info Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Access per-light information

Inputs: - Light Type - Filter: All / Sun / Point / Spot

Outputs: - Direction - Light direction - Distance - Distance to light source - Color - Light color - Energy - Light intensity

Usage: Per-light calculations, conditional lighting effects.

docs.title: Scene Color Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Read scene data in filter materials

Inputs: - UV/Coordinate - Sampling coordinates (default: screen space)

Outputs: - Color - Scene color at that coordinate - Depth - Scene depth value - Normal - Scene normal data

Parameters: - Source - Color / Depth / Normal / Emission / Environment

Usage: Post-process effects, reflections, depth-based effects.

docs.title: Additional Nodes
docs.text:
Other important nodes:

  • Portal In/Out - Portal utility nodes
  • Screenspace Info - View space information
  • World Environment - Access environment
  • World To Tangent - Coordinate transformation
  • Bevel - Edge bevel processing
  • Curvature - Output surface curvature
  • Shader Info - Shader parameter access
  • Render Texture - Sample pre-rendered texture

Tip

For detailed parameters and usage, refer to Blender's official shader node documentation combined with NPR Port extensions.

docs.title: Issue: Scene Color Returns Black
docs.text:
Problem: Scene Color node in Filter returns black

Solution: 1. Check if Filter Material is in the correct execution stage 2. Verify the scene has lights and visible geometry 3. Ensure Window texture coordinates are connected 4. Try switching Scene Color Source option 5. Check if rendering occurs before filter evaluation

docs.title: Issue: Render Texture Not Updating
docs.text:
Problem: Render Texture shows outdated or old data

Solution: 1. Change update mode to "Every Frame" 2. Verify source camera exists and is enabled 3. Check if texture resolution exceeds VRAM 4. Ensure rendering occurs before material sampling 5. If memory-constrained, try lowering resolution

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always use Eevee for NPR Port features
  2. Test in viewport with material preview before final render
  3. Use light groups to organize complex scenes
  4. Monitor VRAM when using multiple render textures
  5. Stack filters efficiently - combine effects where possible
  6. Profile performance - use shader editor timing information

Warning

NPR Port is optimized for Eevee only. Cycles support is limited.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: NPR Tree is a flexible, node-based non-photorealistic rendering pipeline. It supports custom line rendering, toon shading, and artistic effects.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Per-light processing using For Each Light
  • Real-time preview in viewport
  • Built-in node groups for effects (shadows, toon, etc.)
  • Complete shading control

docs.title: NPR Input Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Main input for NPR Tree processing

Outputs (9 total): - Base Color - Material base color - Metallic - Metallic property - Roughness - Surface roughness - Normal - Surface normal - Alpha - Transparency - Emission - Self-emission color - IOR - Index of refraction - Light Direction - Light source direction - Specular - Specular reflection strength

docs.title: For Each Light Node
docs.text:
Purpose: Process rendering for each light source in the scene

Outputs: - Light Index - Current light ID (starting from 0) - Light Direction - Direction from surface to light source - Light Distance - Distance to light source - Light Color - Light color value - Light Energy - Light intensity

Usage Pattern: 

NPR Input → For Each Light → [Calculate per-light effects]
                                → Merge results → Output

Common Uses: - Toon shading with multiple light tones - Per-light cel shading - Multi-pass lighting effects

docs.text:

  • Input: Image, UV coordinates
  • Output: Color, Alpha

docs.title: NPR Refraction
docs.text:

docs.title: Built-in Node Groups
docs.text:
• Cavity - Shadow-based shading
  • Kuwahara Filter - Artistic style smoothing
  • Curvature Shading - Edge-based effects
  • Shading Models - Pre-built toon/stylized shaders

docs.title: Simple Toon Shading Setup
docs.text:
1. Create a material with Principled BSDF
  2. Add NPR Tree node
  3. Inside NPR Tree (Ctrl+Tab):
  4. Connect NPR Input to For Each Light
  5. Sample lighting properties
  6. Apply toon shading from node groups
  7. Merge all light contributions
  8. Output results to material
  9. Render in viewport or final render

Tip: Test with different light configurations for best results.

Warning

NPR Tree is Eevee-exclusive. Not available in Cycles.

docs.title: Feature Description
docs.text:
Render Textures is a scene-level Eevee additional render texture system.

It allows the scene to maintain up to 4 Render Texture slots, each of which can specify a camera and an output type. The scene result from that camera perspective is first rendered into a texture, then sampled in regular object materials through the Render Texture node.

docs.title: Panel Entry Point
docs.text: Scene Properties > Render Textures

docs.title: Configurable Parameters
docs.text:
Each Render Texture entry currently supports:

Parameter Description Name The identifier name of the texture entry for referencing in nodes Enabled Enable/disable rendering of this texture Source Choose what to capture: Color / Depth / Normal Camera Specify the camera for rendering this texture Resolution X/Y Output texture pixel dimensions Update Mode Update frequency: Every Sample / Every Frame / Manual Format Output precision: RGBA16F / RGBA32F / R16F / R32F

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
1. Open Scene Properties > Render Textures
  2. Create a new entry
  3. Select Source, Camera, resolution and format
  4. Add a Render Texture node in object materials
  5. Select the corresponding entry in the node panel
  6. Use the node output in material calculations

Tip

Perfect for creating real-time reflections, screen-space effects, and dynamic textures.

docs.title: Feature Description
docs.text: It is a set of scene-level Eevee full-screen filter stack. Each entry is a Filter domain material that processes the current frame in list order.

docs.title: Panel Entry Point
docs.text:
Scene Properties > Filter Materials

Node tree entry point: Shader Node Editor > Shader Type > Filter

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
1. Open Scene Properties > Filter Materials
  2. Create a new entry
  3. The selected material must be a Filter domain material
  4. Open Shader Editor and switch the top Shader Type to Filter
  5. Use Scene Color to read scene data
  6. Output the result with Filter Output
  7. Select filter execution position via Execution Stage

docs.title: Execution Stages
docs.text:
• Before Volume Fog - Execute before volume fog processing
  • Before Depth of Field - Execute before depth of field
  • Before Composite - Execute before compositing

Note

Filter Materials can only use Filter domain materials.

Use Cases

  • Color grading and tone mapping
  • Screen-space effects (e.g., edge detection, toon rendering)
  • Motion blur and motion vector effects
  • Post-process denoising and sharpening
